claims.text: The investigated alloy is additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA.
The additively manufactured alloy has enhanced strength.
In-situ electron microscopy during oxidation will reveal significant elemental redistribution in the alloy.
In-situ electron microscopy during oxidation will reveal changes in nanoprecipitate morphology.
Observing elemental redistribution and nanoprecipitate morphology will enhance understanding of the alloy's oxidation behavior.
The relevant oxidation conditions are high-temperature environments typical of gas turbines, power plants, and aerospace components.
Nanoprecipitates are present within the HEA matrix.
In-situ electron microscopy permits real-time observation of oxidation processes.
In-situ electron microscopy permits real-time observation of elemental redistribution in nanoprecipitates.
Specific elemental changes in nanoprecipitates will correlate with oxidation resistance.
Specific morphological adaptations of nanoprecipitates will correlate with oxidation resistance.
The current understanding of oxidation behavior is based on cast and wrought counterparts.
Results from this alloy may not generalize to all HEAs or other alloy systems.
The extent of elemental redistribution and its impact on oxidation behavior are uncertain until experimentally observed.
Absence of significant elemental redistribution and nanoprecipitate morphological changes during oxidation would falsify the hypothesis.
